name: Range Resources Corporation

profile.description: Range Resources Corporation is an independent natural gas and NGL producer focused exclusively on the Appalachian Basin, primarily the Marcellus Shale in southwestern Pennsylvania. The company produced approximately 2.35-2.40 Bcfe/d in 2025 and generated approximately $400 million in free cash flow in Q1 2026 alone. Range pioneered horizontal drilling in the Marcellus Shale and maintains one of the largest acreage positions in the formation. Founded in 1976, headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (0/3): Range Resources remains a pure-play Appalachian natural gas producer with no meaningful product launches, market pivots, or business model transformations in the last 5 years [1]. Revenue growth of 22% YoY in Q1 2026 is entirely driven by higher natural gas commodity prices, not innovation. The company drills wells, produces gas, and sells it — the same model for decades. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or quantified AI-driven operational improvements reported. Market Share (1/2): Range is one of the largest independent natural gas producers in the Marcellus Shale with significant acreage position, achieving its best quarterly natural gas differential in over a decade at $0.18 premium to Henry Hub in Q1 2026 [1]. However, EQT is the clear Appalachian gas leader by production volume. Product Pipeline (1/2): 300 MMcf/d processing expansion coming online mid-2026 targeting 2.5 Bcfe/d year-end 2026 production, with 2027 guidance of ~2.6 Bcfe/d — these are specific capacity expansion milestones with defined timelines [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): E&P companies do not have traditional R&D budgets; capital expenditure of $650-700M for 2026 represents drilling and completion investment, not R&D.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Range Resources' purpose centers on responsible natural gas production and American energy security — a generic E&P mission interchangeable with any competitor in the basin. No distinctive vision of a future state that inspires beyond profitable gas extraction [3]. Community Impact (0/2): Range Resources pleaded no contest to environmental crimes at southwestern Pennsylvania well sites in 2020, paying $150,000 in fines for leaks and spills including a 2,000-gallon fracking waste leak into a creek [3]. Residents near Range wells reported contaminated drinking water, hydrogen sulfide odors, and health complaints. While the company has since published sustainability reports, the documented environmental violations and community health impacts preclude a positive community impact score. Employee Retention (0/2): Approximately 565 employees with no specific retention, tenure, or turnover data publicly available. Insider Buying (0/2): Net insider selling of $1.0M in the last 3 months with no insider buying activity identified; insiders have only sold shares recently [4].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics — all core and growth metrics at or above targets. Q1 2026 delivered $1.03B revenue (up 22% YoY) with net income of $341.6M (up 253%) and approximately $400M free cash flow [1]. Unit margin per Mcfe of $2.77 increased 38% YoY reflecting higher realized prices and favorable contract structure. D/E of 20% is exceptionally conservative for an E&P, well below the 70% target. ROE of 21.13% exceeds the 15% target [4]. Profit margin of 33% significantly exceeds the 20% target, driven by gas price recovery to $4.05 strip for 2026. Forward P/E of 9.85 is deeply discounted below the 20 target. Forward PEG of 0.64 indicates the market expects significant earnings growth at an attractive price [4]. Revenue growth of 22% YoY and estimated 5-year CAGR of ~11% both exceed targets. Liquidity floor cleared: 4M daily volume x $36.35 = $145.4M [4].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Natural gas production is a physical-world operation involving subsurface geology, horizontal drilling, hydraulic fracturing, pipeline infrastructure, and processing facilities that AI structurally cannot displace [1]. AI data center expansion is a direct demand tailwind — power generation for AI facilities requires vast amounts of natural gas, and Range Resources' Marcellus Shale position near East Coast data center clusters (Northern Virginia, New Jersey) is strategically valuable. The combination of physical operations, regulatory permitting requirements, and infrastructure moats makes this business essentially immune to AI disruption. AI Opportunity (0/1): Range Resources does not generate revenue from AI-related products or services. The company is an indirect AI beneficiary through increased gas demand but does not sell AI infrastructure or services directly.

infinite_game.summary: Range Resources plays a predominantly finite game — it exists to extract natural gas profitably from Appalachian wells and return capital to shareholders. The company's strategy is entirely commodity-price dependent, with no articulated vision beyond efficient resource extraction. Sinek would note that Range endures through commodity cycles (50 years of operation) but questions whether survival through inertia constitutes infinite game thinking. The environmental violations and lack of a distinctive purpose suggest a company optimizing for the current quarter rather than building toward a future that doesn't yet exist.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Range Resources articulates a standard E&P mission around responsible natural gas production and American energy security [3]. This purpose is interchangeable with any E&P peer — Devon, EQT, Southwestern, or Coterra could use identical language. It describes what the company does, not why it matters beyond profit. No evidence that strategic decisions are guided by a deeper purpose.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Range operates as a lean 565-employee organization with experienced Appalachian Basin operating teams and stable leadership under CEO Dennis Degner [1]. The small team size and focused geographic footprint likely create strong working relationships. No evidence of major cultural problems, leadership instability, or high turnover. However, no specific evidence of exceptional trust or employee empowerment either.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Range Resources' competitive positioning focuses on being the low-cost Marcellus Shale producer and achieving premium gas differentials to Henry Hub [1]. Competitive language centers on outperforming peers on unit costs and realizations rather than learning from rivals' strengths. EQT, the basin leader, is treated as a competitor to beat rather than a worthy rival to learn from.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): Range Resources remains a pure-play Appalachian natural gas producer with no evidence of strategic diversification, business model adaptation, or willingness to pivot [1]. The company has produced gas from the same basin for decades with no exploration of adjacent markets, energy transition investments, or transformative strategic shifts. This rigidity could become existential if natural gas demand structurally declines.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Range has maintained disciplined capital allocation through natural gas price volatility — continuing to invest $650-700M annually in drilling programs while generating significant free cash flow ($400M in Q1 2026 alone) rather than cutting to zero during downturns [1]. The Board's 11.1% dividend increase during a period of commodity uncertainty shows confidence in the production base. However, these decisions carry limited relative risk given the company's clean balance sheet (D/E 20%) and strong cash generation.

investment_thesis: Range Resources delivered exceptional Q1 2026 results with $1.03B revenue (up 22% YoY), net income of $341.6M (up 253%), and approximately $400M in free cash flow driven by improved natural gas pricing ($4.05 strip for 2026) and best-in-decade gas differentials at $0.18 premium to Henry Hub [1]. At a forward P/E of 9.85 and PEG of 0.64, the stock is deeply discounted with every fundamental metric at or above target levels — 33% profit margin, 21% ROE, 20% D/E. The 300 MMcf/d processing expansion mid-2026 targeting 2.5 Bcfe/d production provides near-term growth visibility, and AI data center power demand creates a secular tailwind for Appalachian natural gas situated near major East Coast population and data center clusters [1][4].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on commodity dependence and lack of diversification. Range Resources is a single-basin, single-commodity producer whose profitability is entirely dependent on Henry Hub and Appalachian gas pricing — a sustained decline to sub-$3 Henry Hub would severely compress the current 33% margins [1]. The stock dropped from $48.31 to $36.35 (25% decline) in the past year despite improving earnings, reflecting market skepticism about commodity price sustainability. Environmental violations (2020 no-contest plea to environmental crimes, $150K fine for fracking waste spills) create reputational and regulatory risk in an increasingly scrutinized industry [3]. The 1.1% dividend yield provides minimal downside protection, and the pure-play strategy offers no diversification against long-term energy transition risks. Innovation and inspiration scores reflect the reality that Range is a well-optimized commodity extraction machine, not a company with a transformative purpose or innovative business model [4].
key_catalysts: 300 MMcf/d processing expansion mid-2026 driving production toward 2.5 Bcfe/d, with 2027 guidance of ~2.6 Bcfe/d providing visible production growth trajectory [1]
AI data center power demand creating sustained natural gas consumption growth, with Range's proximity to East Coast data center clusters (Northern Virginia, New Jersey) providing geographic advantage
Continued free cash flow generation (~$400M Q1 alone) enabling balance sheet improvement, dividend growth, and share repurchases at discounted valuation [1]
key_risks: Natural gas price volatility — single commodity exposure means a sustained Henry Hub decline below $3.00 would compress margins from 33% to low single digits, eliminating the entire financial thesis [1]
Single-basin concentration — 100% Marcellus/Appalachian exposure creates geological, regulatory, and pipeline infrastructure concentration risk with no geographic diversification

Environmental and regulatory risk — documented environmental crimes ($150K fine in 2020 for fracking waste spills), community health complaints, and increasing regulatory scrutiny of Appalachian drilling could increase compliance costs or restrict operations [3]
